questions.prompt: A territorial map displays treaty lines, military occupation, Indigenous homelands, and later state boundaries. What is the strongest historical use of the map?
choices: Assume a boundary drawn by a government proves all people within it consented.
Use the overlapping layers to distinguish legal claims, military control, settlement, and sovereignty rather than treating them as identical.
Treat later state borders as the only relevant geography.
Conclude that mapped borders make questions of removal and sovereignty unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Political boundaries, occupation, settlement, and sovereignty are distinct historical realities and should not be collapsed into one map layer.
